title: Floor division from C's truncating division
hints: C's `/` rounds toward zero. Floor rounds toward negative infinity. When do those two disagree?
They only disagree when the exact quotient is negative and not a whole number. Start from `q = a / b` and fix it up in that case.

The quotient is negative when `a` and `b` have opposite signs, and inexact when `a % b != 0`. In exactly that case, subtract 1 from `q`. In C, `(a < 0) != (b < 0)` is true exactly when the signs differ.

answer.explain: Truncation and floor agree except when the true quotient is a negative non-integer, where truncation lands one too high. The solution detects that case with `a % b != 0` and opposite signs, and subtracts 1. That's why `-7 / 2` becomes -4 instead of C's -3.
